title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA)
what: The Pazin State Archive holds the parish registers of central Istria. Two letters to this family, of 26 April and 24 June 2021, enclosed the certified copy of Josip Defranceschi's 1863 baptism and prints from the Status Animarum of Gallignana for the households of Antonius and of Giovanni Battista.
cites: MKR župe Gračišće 1841–1899, entry 23 of 1863
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01071656
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01072071
Church books ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215, Gologorica, Gračišće and Lindar
note: They charge for research and will search, certify and post a named record. The two 2021 requests cost 117 and 124 kuna including overseas postage.

title: Arolsen Archives — International Center on Nazi Persecution
what: The former International Tracing Service. Holds the wartime and displaced-persons records of some seventeen and a half million people, and 79 records under this surname — many more than the family's own copy of file D-1.505. Mined to the bottom in September 2026: the Reutlingen town list of Yugoslav nationals, the wartime sickness-fund cards in their original colour, the IRO care-and-maintenance file, and the whole of displaced-persons folder DP0758 — nineteen French occupation cards for the two brothers' households, holding Petar's photograph, the day Zdravko's family sailed for Australia, and Luise's statelessness.
cites: DP folder DP0758, reference 03010101 05 070 — nineteen cards, IRO 148.901 and 148.902
Counselling card, category CB, 28.4.51, with the entries of 22.7.49, 28.4.51 and 25.5.51
Carte d'identité de personnes déplacées no. 30040, issued 27 November 1946 to Lujza Defranceski
Tracing and documentation case no. 349.822, reference 06030302.0.349.822, 8 documents, 1954–1984 — withheld online
Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR, CM/1 files from Germany (3.2.1.1), 6 documents
note: Access requires accepting a declaration about sensitive personal data; the account holder must do that himself. Person rows in the search results are click handlers, not links, and the page images sit on a separate server that requires a referer header. The T/D tracing case is the one substantial thing still unread: eight documents spanning 1954 to 1984, withheld online for data protection and obtainable only by written request to Bad Arolsen.

title: Hrvatski državni arhiv
what: The Croatian State Archive. HDA 583 is the Pisino (Pazin) marriage register in which Carlo De Franceschi signs as a witness on 13 September 1842, giving his rank as I. R. Auscultans.
cites: HDA 583, Pisino marriages 1842–43

title: Matične knjige — Croatian parish registers
what: The baptism of Ana Kalanj at Ledenice on 3 January 1864; the baptism of Anton Rudolf at Klenovica on 20 January 1890, which gives the parents' place of origin as Gallignana in Istria; the marriage of Nodburga Defranceschi at Bakar on 27 February 1794.
note: Held as scans by the family.

title: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli and Comune di Concesio — atti di morte
what: Italian civil death registers: Pietro De Franceschi, mason, aged 44, in the civic hospital at San Daniele on 30 March 1895; Edoardo De Franceschi, former officer of Zara, aged 48, in the same hospital on 12 August 1899; Giovanni De Franceschi, aged three, at Concesio above Brescia on 15 July 1916.
cites: San Daniele del Friuli, atti di morte no. 19 (1895) and no. 28 (1899)
Concesio, atti di morte, parte II serie A (1916)

title: Antenati — Portale degli Antenati
what: The Italian state archives' genealogy portal. The Archivio di Stato di Udine has 49,184 registers on it, including 6,693 for the communes of the Tolmezzo tribunal — that is Carnia — and fifty-nine for the Comune di Mione alone. The three De Franceschi birth acts of 1809–1810 at Mione and Muina come from there.
cites: Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1809 e 1810
Nati, indice 1806–1810, sig. 12954
note: Its name search sits behind a bot check, which this archive does not bypass. Browsing the registers by place and year needs no such thing, and the images are served openly over IIIF — which is how these were read.

title: FamilySearch
what: The single largest source in this archive. Its collection «Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994» (cc 2040054) supplied the burial and baptism entries; its persona search supplied the household reconstructions, the emigrant records and the four children of Josip and Ana Kalanj; its catalogue supplied the parish-book inventory.
cites: Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994 (cc 2040054)
note: Free with an account. Only about a quarter of that collection is name-indexed; the rest is images to be read. Nothing was bulk-downloaded.

title: Find a Grave
what: Ninety-six memorials under every spelling of the surname, from which the grave gazetteer is built. Each name on that page links to its own memorial.
note: A volunteer index, heavily weighted to the English-speaking world and Italy. Croatia is almost absent from it, and the count of one Croatian grave is a fact about the index before it is a fact about the family.

title: Wikimedia Commons
what: Four public-domain works reproduced on the namesakes page: Titian's portrait of Andrea de' Franceschi (Detroit Institute of Arts); the Vasari woodcut of Piero della Francesca from the 1648 Vite; Piero's Urbino diptych; and Mariano de Franceschi's Camel Caravan at Rest.
note: Each file is credited and linked on the namesakes page itself.

title: Lee Steiner, Croatia Church Books — mapped
what: A set of Google Earth overlays mapping every Croatian parish register in the FamilySearch collection to its place, with the browse link for each. Used to inventory what survives on film for Crikvenica, Ledenice, Novi Vinodolski, Grižane, Selce, Senj and Fužine.
note: Held in the family's own files as .kmz.

title: Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria: note storiche»
what: The family's own historian on his own country. The full text is in the family's papers.

title: «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler»
where: Atti e Memorie della Società Istriana, 1928
what: The letters in which Carlo, about 1873, sets out what his family believed about itself: that it came from Carnia and settled in Istria «intorno al 1700»; that De Franceschi still lived at Mione and Muina; that his trisavolo Giambattista built the 1711 house at Gologorica; and the blazon of the family arms.
note: The single most important narrative source in this archive.

title: Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino»
what: Carlo's son on the county the family lived in — still the standard work. With his editions of the Labin statutes, the Piran chartulary and «Gli Artizoni di Parenzo».
note: Some of the primary sources Camillo used were destroyed in the Second World War and its aftermath. For those documents his articles are now the only witness.

title: Blasonario Giuliano
what: The armorial of Venezia Giulia. Its entry «Franceschi (De) — Pisino, Moncalvo, Pola» names Carlo and Camillo and gives the family's arms; a separate entry covers the Seghetto, Capodistria and Umago branch, and others the Capodistria and Ližnjan families.
cites: Blasonario_D.pdf
Blasonario_F.pdf
note: The blazon of the Moncalvo arms is credited to «(C. de F.)» — Carlo himself — with Benedetti and de Totto supplying the tinctures. It formalises his testimony rather than confirming it independently.

title: Petar Puhmajer, «Stancija de Franceschi u Segetu kod Umaga»
what: The conservation monograph on the Seget estate: how it was bought from the Valier in 1720, how the house was built and rebuilt, and the two Istrian branches.

title: «La tenuta de Franceschi di Seghetto», la Voce del popolo
what: The Italian-language daily of Rijeka on the Seget estate: the county in Crete, the 1538 defence of Calus, Lemiores and Sabionera, the shipwreck of 1669, the hundred thousand ducats of 1716, the library of four thousand volumes and its destruction, and the arms on the tympanum. Photographs by Gianfranco Abrami.
note: Where it and the Blasonario disagree on a date, the armorial is preferred and the difference is stated.

title: Deborah Howard, «Titian's Portraits of Grand Chancellor Andrea de' Franceschi»
what: The life of Andrea de' Franceschi, born 1473, Grand Chancellor of Venice from 15 September 1529 until his death in 1552, buried at Santi Giovanni e Paolo — his embassies, his will and its five codicils, and the Titian portraits he left his nephew.

title: Josip Banić, «Venetian Istria in the Embrace of a Nascent Dominium (c. 1381 – c. 1470)»
what: A modern historian's verdict on Camillo: one of three figures who «tower» over Istrian medieval studies, and the only surviving witness to sources lost in the war. Quotes Egidio Ivetic that for medieval Istria one must rely on Benussi, Carlo De Franceschi and De Vergottini.

title: Centro di Ricerche Storiche di Rovigno — catalogue of Istrian sacred art
what: Catalogues the paintings in the chapel of Stancija Seghetto — formerly Villa De Franceschi — and records their poor condition; and a Pentecost whose patron Antonio Alisi identified as «un de Franceschi nobile di Seghetto».

title: Hrvatski plemićki zbor — the Franceschi family
what: The Croatian Noble Corps on the Zadar and Omiš descent: Niccolò received into the Hungarian-Croatian nobility by charter at Buda in 1359; the branch at Omiš from Francesca de Franceschi in the later sixteenth century; Giovanni «il Zuane» and the siege of Imotski in 1718.

title: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani
what: The biographies of Carlo De Franceschi, Camillo De Franceschi and Girolamo de' Franceschi of Koper, bishop of Corone.

title: Diocesan and press notices for Mons. Lucio Soravito de Franceschi
where: Arcidiocesi di Udine; Cathopedia; Messaggero Veneto
what: Born at Mione di Ovaro on 8 December 1939, ordained 1963, Bishop of Adria-Rovigo 2004–2015, died 6 July 2019. The evidence that the surname was still in the village of the 1679 headmen's list two hundred and sixty years later.

title: «The DeFranceschi Family Tree Album»
where: printed for the first family reunion, Crystal Springs Resort, 7–9 September 2012
what: The American branch's own history and chart, headed «started by Antonio DeFranceschi 8/6/1856 – 10/23/1924 + Maria Valhart 4/6/1867 – 1945». Eleven children, five countries. Also the description of the arms carved on the 1711 house at Moncalvo.
note: Assembled from Anton Rumac's handwritten notes and a cassette tape made by cousin Bruno. Its compiler says plainly there will be errors; where it can be checked against registers, it holds.

title: The family's MacFamilyTree file
what: A database of 281 people and 247 photographs, catalogued and captioned by the family. The source of every portrait on this site of the Crikvenica house, and of the photographs of three graves.
note: Where it conflicts with a register — Zdravko's death year, Josip's wife — the register is preferred and the conflict is stated on the page.

title: defranceski.com
what: The roster of significant persons, the account of the four Croatian lines, the collected blazons, and the descent chart that first set out the line from Giovanni of Gologorica to Brisbane.
note: This archive absorbs its content rather than duplicating it; its hosted images are token-gated and could not be fetched, so equivalent public-domain works were sourced from Wikimedia Commons instead.

title: The Omiš and Seget photographs
what: Studio portraits of the Omiš branch — Josip and Anna with baby Ante, Zane, Frane, Anton «Toni» of 1932 — and seven photographs of the Seget villa: the 1843 façade, the tympanum with its carved arms, the crenellated tower, the rustic range and the well.

title: MyHeritage family tree export, July 2018
what: A GEDCOM of 8,286 individuals, 254 of them carrying this surname, compiled by the family on MyHeritage and grown by that site's Smart Matching and by Geni's SmartCopy through 2017. Two very different things are inside it. Its Crikvenica and Blažević entries are first-hand family knowledge — dates off gravestones and the backs of photographs — and they are the archive's only source for nine of the people on this site, including Anton's birth at Reutlingen on 22 August 1944. Its Dalmatian and Venetian upper reaches are a compiled noble pedigree with no register citations, and it joins that pedigree to this family in error.
cites: Anton Defranceski, b. 22 August 1944 Reutlingen, d. 28 June 1999 Ipswich
Ruža Hreljac, b. 13 February 1922 Fužine, d. 30 January 1996 Horsham
Hedviga Blažević, b. 8 March 1926 Senj, d. 30 October 2001 Johannesburg
Ivan Defranceski, b. 25 June 1925 Crikvenica, d. 30 October 1995 Senj
Josip «Pepe» Defranceski 1911–1980 and Božica Blašković 1911–1994
note: Read with care and read to the bottom. The seam where the two families are joined is set out on the Imotski page; below it the file is the best source the archive has for the twentieth-century household. Its narrative notes on the Imotski family are quoted from stariimotski.com, credited there to the archive of Captain Vjeko Franceschi.
